reading.body:
DataBank SLC6 publishes 22 MW of IT capacity, the largest single published figure among Utah's three facilities with stated power specs, though most facilities in the state publish no power data at all.

The 22 MW footprint translates to roughly 2,200 racks at standard colocation density or 550 racks at AI training density, depending on which power profile the facility actually serves. DataBank does not publish its cooling architecture, power redundancy tier, or split between available and committed capacity, so the true headroom for new workloads cannot be determined from the operator's public specifications alone. This opacity is common across the data center sector and makes capacity planning for power-constrained regions difficult.

SLC6's rank as Utah's largest published facility reflects only what operators choose to disclose. The state has 21 mapped facilities total, but 18 of them publish no megawatt figures. The three that do report 39 MW combined. This gap between published and actual capacity means regional power availability for AI infrastructure cannot be assessed from operator disclosures without field-level investigation or regulatory filings that transcend marketing websites.
